types.embedding_query_text: GeographicRegion: A geographic area with defined boundaries. Also called Territory, Area, Region. Examples: Gaza, Gaza Strip.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: Best match for geographic area with defined boundaries.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state with its own government. Also called Nation, State, Republic. Examples: Israel.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a sovereign state.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitantGroup: An organization that uses violence to achieve its goals. Also called Terrorist Organization, Insurgent Group, Rebel Group. Examples: Hamas.

chosen_type.label: MilitantGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organization that uses violence to achieve its goals.
chosen_type.justification: No suitable schema.org type for militant groups.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

types.embedding_query_text: Market: A place where goods or services are bought and sold. Also called Bazaar, Shopping Center, Trade Center. Examples: Al-Balata market.

chosen_type.label: Market
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a place where goods or services are bought and sold.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: OnlineMarketplace
candidates.comment: An OnlineMarketplace, as an OnlineStore, is an e-commerce platform where multiple sellers offer products or services. Also called e-marketplace, digital marketplace, online bazaar. Examples: Amazon, eBay, Etsy. Distinct from OnlineStore, which is a single seller's e-commerce site.

candidates.label: SellAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent exchanging goods or services for money with a buyer. Also called selling, vending, trading, transacting. Examples: a store selling a product to a customer, a person selling a used car, a company selling software licenses. Distinct from BuyAction, which is the reciprocal act from the buyer's perspective.

types.embedding_query_text: RefugeeCamp: A temporary settlement for people who have been displaced from their homes. Also called Displacement Camp, Internally Displaced Persons Camp, IDP Camp. Examples: Nuseirat refugee camp.

chosen_type.label: RefugeeCamp
chosen_type.definition: A temporary settlement for people who have been displaced from their homes.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for refugee camps.

candidates.label: Accommodation
candidates.comment: An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence. Examples: A hotel suite, a campsite, a vacation rental apartment, a conference room.

candidates.label: CampingPitch
candidates.comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.

candidates.label: Campground
candidates.comment: A Campground is a CivicStructure or place used for overnight outdoor stays, typically containing multiple individual camping pitches for tents or recreational vehicles. Also called camping site, campsite, RV park, caravan park. Examples: Yellowstone National Park Campground, KOA Campground, a local state park campsite. Distinct from Hotel, which provides indoor lodging.

candidates.label: AnimalShelter
candidates.comment: An AnimalShelter is a LocalBusiness that provides temporary housing and care for animals, often facilitating adoption. Also called animal rescue, humane society, pet shelter. Examples: The ASPCA, a local humane society, a dog rescue organization.

candidates.label: BuddhistTemple
candidates.comment: A BuddhistTemple is a PlaceOfWorship dedicated to Buddhist religious practices and ceremonies. Also called pagoda, wat, vihara, dharma center. Examples: Wat Arun, Todai-ji Temple, a local Zen center.

types.embedding_query_text: Mosque: A building where Muslims worship and gather for community events. Also called Islamic Center, Masjid, Place of Worship. Examples: Ahmad Yassin Mosque.

chosen_type.label: Mosque
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a Muslim place of worship.

candidates.label: Mosque
candidates.comment: A civic structure that is a place of worship for Muslims. Also called masjid, Islamic house of worship, Islamic center. Examples: "Blue Mosque", "Faisal Mosque", a local community mosque. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a broader category.

candidates.label: Synagogue
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a Jewish house of worship and often a center for community activities. Also called Jewish temple, shul, house of prayer. Examples: 'The Great Synagogue of Rome', a local community synagogue.

candidates.label: Church
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a place of worship for Christian congregations. Also called house of God, chapel, sanctuary, temple (Christian context). Examples: Westminster Abbey, a local Baptist church, a small village chapel. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a general term for any religious building.

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: HinduTemple
candidates.comment: A HinduTemple is a place of worship and civic structure dedicated to Hindu deities. Also called Mandir, Hindu shrine, temple. Examples: Akshardham Temple, Sri Venkateswara Temple, a local Hindu community temple.

types.embedding_query_text: Hospital: A healthcare facility that provides medical treatment and care. Also called Medical Center, Healthcare Facility, Clinic. Examples: Al-Awda Hospital.

chosen_type.label: Hospital
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a healthcare facility.

candidates.label: Hospital
candidates.comment: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: A company or institution that gathers and disseminates news and information. Also called Media Outlet, News Agency, Publishing Company. Examples: Al Jazeera.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a company that gathers and disseminates news.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: Journalist: A person who researches and writes news stories for a media outlet. Also called Reporter, Correspondent, News Writer. Examples: Hani Mahmoud.

chosen_type.label: Journalist
chosen_type.definition: A person who writes about news and current events.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for journalists.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: Article
candidates.comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryOrganization: A group of people who are trained to fight and defend a country or organization. Also called Armed Forces, Defense Force, Military Force. Examples: Israeli military, Israel Defense Forces.

chosen_type.label: MilitaryOrganization
chosen_type.definition: A group of people trained to fight and defend a country or organization.
chosen_type.justification: No suitable schema.org type for military organizations.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsAgency: A company or institution that gathers and disseminates news and information to other media outlets. Also called Wire Service, News Service, Press Agency. Examples: AFP, Agence France-Presse.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a news agency.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

candidates.label: RadioStation
candidates.comment: A RadioStation is a LocalBusiness representing an organization that broadcasts radio content. Also called radio broadcaster, radio company. Examples: WNYC, BBC Radio, a local commercial radio station, a public radio station.

types.embedding_query_text: School: An institution where children and adults can receive education and training. Also called Educational Institution, Learning Center, Academy. Examples: Abu Tammam School.

chosen_type.label: School
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for an educational institution.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: HighSchool
candidates.comment: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

candidates.label: ElementarySchool
candidates.comment: An ElementarySchool is an EducationalOrganization providing primary education. Also called primary school, grade school. Examples: Oakwood Elementary School, P.S. 123, a local junior school.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large human settlement with a fixed boundary and a local government. Also called Metropolis, Municipality, Urban Area. Examples: Beit Lahia, Khan Younis, Gaza City.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a large human settlement.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: Town: A smaller human settlement with a fixed boundary and a local government. Also called Village, Municipality, Rural Area. Examples: Az-Zawayda.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Although 'town' is mentioned, City is the closest match in schema.org.

candidates.label: City

Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea

candidates.label: DaySpa
candidates.comment: A local business offering health and beauty services, typically without overnight accommodation. Also called Spa, beauty spa, wellness center. Examples: "The Serene Spa", "Urban Retreat Day Spa", "Relaxation Station". Distinct from HealthClub, which focuses more on fitness and exercise facilities.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A point or area in space where something is situated or takes place. Also called Place, Site, Area. Examples: Al-Sawarha.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a point or area in space.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchGroup: An organization that conducts research and analysis on a specific topic or issue. Also called Think Tank, Research Institute, Analysis Group. Examples: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, ACLED.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for an organization conducting research.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

types.embedding_query_text: Newspaper: A publication that contains news, articles, and advertisements, typically published on a daily or weekly basis. Also called Newspaper Publication, Daily Newspaper, Weekly Newspaper. Examples: Haaretz.

chosen_type.label: Newspaper
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for a publication containing news and articles.

candidates.label: Newspaper
candidates.comment: A Newspaper, as a Periodical, is a publication containing information about varied topics, often published daily. Also called daily paper, news publication, gazette. Examples: The Wall Street Journal, The Guardian, a local community newspaper. Distinct from Magazine, which is typically published weekly or monthly with a specific focus.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle

candidates.label: Article

Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

candidates.label: OpinionNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An OpinionNewsArticle, as a NewsArticle, primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. Also called opinion piece, editorial, column. types.embedding_query_text: Group Examples: Palestinian mourners, civilians.

chosen_type.label: Crowd

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Cemetery

candidates.label: Crematorium

candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. types.embedding_query_text: Organization Examples: Palestinian group.

chosen_type.label: Organization

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

chosen_type.label: FuneralProcession
chosen_type.definition: An event where people gather to mourn and pay respects to the deceased.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for funeral processions.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: Crematorium
candidates.comment: A Crematorium is a civic structure where human remains are cremated. Also called crematory, funeral pyre facility. Examples: Golders Green Crematorium, a local funeral home with cremation services.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.
